brief: The canvas depicts an aged, yellowed sheet of newsprint, meticulously filled with fine, wet black ink. The ink forms handwritten script and detailed diagrammatic renderings, making the piece appear like a forgotten personal diary from the 1920s. These diagrams are not random notes, but highly specialized depictions of horizontal mineral stratification, showing distinct layered strata of geologic deposits. The color palette is restricted to the sepia tones of the aged paper and the deep black of the ink. The composition is complex and academic, presenting a silent, static view into a scientific history, inviting the viewer to study its delicate, drawn structure.

statement: This sketch presents a meticulously detailed geological cross-section rendered on aged newsprint, evoking the feel of a personal diary from the 1920s. The composition features horizontal layers of mineral strata in sepia tones, each with distinctive patterns of stripes, dots, or waves that suggest the complex nature of geological formations. The black ink appears wet and deliberate, mimicking the careful handwriting found in historical scientific documents. Subtle paper texture and scattered handwritten annotations reinforce the vintage, personal nature of the document, inviting viewers to examine the intricate details of the stratified geological record as if uncovering a forgotten scientific journal.
